---
title: "Introduction to Quantum Computing — Review"
---

## Essential definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| Quantum Computing | Calculation based on quantum mechanics, not classical physics |
| Quantum Mechanics (Quantum Mechanics) | Description of nature at the subatomic level |
| Qubit | Quantum unit of information (≠ classical bit) |
| Quantum Supremacy | Demonstration that a QC accomplishes a classically infeasible task |
| NISQ | Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum — current era (~100 qubits, noisy) |
| Quantum Error Correction | Technique for managing noise and errors in quantum systems |
| Fault-Tolerant QC | QC capable of correcting errors faster than they occur |

---

## Quantum effects exploited

- **Superposition** (Superposition) — a qubit in several states simultaneously
- **Entanglement** — non-classical correlations between qubits
- **Interference** (Interference) — amplification of correct answers, suppression of incorrect ones

::: {.callout-warning title="Frequent trap"}
A QC **does not test all solutions in parallel** — it exploits interference in a targeted way.
:::

---

## The exponentiality of quantum mechanics

- State of $N$ particles $\Rightarrow$ vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^N}$
- For $N \approx 300$: $2^N \gg 10^{82}$ (> atoms of the universe)
- Exact classical simulation = **impossible** in practice

$$|\psi\rangle \in \mathbb{C}^{2^N}$$

---

## Key quantum algorithms

| Algorithm | Acceleration type | Target problem |
|---|---|---|
| **Shor** | Exponential | Integer factorization → breaks RSA |
| **Grover** | Quadratic ($O(N) \to O(\sqrt{N})$) | Unstructured search |
| **VQE** | Variational (NISQ) | Chemistry/physics simulation |
| **QAOA** | Classical-quantum hybrid | Combinatorial optimization |
| **HHL** | Exponential (conditions) | Linear systems |

---

## What QCs can/can NOT do

| Affirmation | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Solve by testing all possibilities | ❌ FALSE |
| Solve TSP quickly | ❌ FALSE (probably) |
| Factor efficiently (Shor's algo) | ✅ YES |
| Solve all hard NP problems | ❌ FALSE |
| Advantage on certain structured problems | ✅ YES |
| Simulate Quantum Physics/Chemistry | ✅ YES (probable benefit) |
| Solving climate change | ⚠️ UNCERTAIN |

---

## Historical timeline

- **~1930** — 1st quantum revolution: foundations of QM
- **1981** — Feynman: *"Can probabilistic computers simulate QM?"* → **NO**
- **1985** — Deutsch: 1st problem solved faster on QC (constant factor)
- **1992** — Bernstein-Vazirani, Simon: **super-polynomial** advantage
- **1994** — **Shor**: factorization → RSA and Diffie-Hellman threat
- **~2017** — Transition from ~10 to ~200 qubits, start of NISQ era
- **2019** — Google: quantum supremacy (Sycamore, 53 qubits)
- **2021** — Chinese Academy of Sciences: classical reproduction via tensor networks (512 GPUs, 3 p.m.)
- **~2030+** — Horizon: fault-tolerant quantum computing

---

## Types of physical qubits

- Persistent current in superconducting circuit ← **Google, IBM**
- Photon polarization
- Electronic spin (magnetic field)
- Internal state of atom (trapped ions)

---

## Classic strategies to circumvent QM complexity

| Strategy | Examples |
|---|---|
| Analytical approximations | Bethe ansatz, Feynman diagrams, disturbance theory, mean field |
| Numerical simulations | DFT, Quantum Monte Carlo |
| Favorable systems | Quasi-classical, weakly correlated systems |

## Relations between concepts
```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    QM["Mécanique Quantique"] --> SP["Superposition"]
    QM --> ENT["Enchevêtrement"]
    QM --> INT["Interférence"]
    SP & ENT & INT --> QC["Ordinateur Quantique"]
    QC --> SHOR["Algo de Shor\n(factorisation)"]
    QC --> GROVER["Algo de Grover\n(recherche)"]
    QC --> SIM["Simulation quantique"]
    QC --> NISQ["Dispositifs NISQ\n(VQE, QAOA)"]
```

---

## Critical points to remember

::: {.callout-important title="Cryptographic impact"}
Shor breaks **RSA** and **Diffie-Hellman** → Internet security threatened as soon as a fault-tolerant QC exists.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Quantum-inspired"}
Thinking quantumly has value **even classically** — e.g. Tang algorithm (2018) inspired by Kerenidis-Prakash, reaching $\mathcal{O}(\text{poly}\log(mn))$ classically.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="NISQ ≠ guaranteed benefit"}
Current NISQ devices cannot run Shor. The practical advantage on real problems remains to be demonstrated.
:::
